I hold rather than trade for three reasons. (1) The fundamental thesis is not what broke: hyperscaler capex is going UP (Alphabet 2027 >$300B, Amazon raised again), Micron's HBM is sold out for 2026 under take-or-pay contracts, and AWS capacity is sold out into 2027; that is the demand for exactly these chips, memory, foundry and switches. (2) A replacement book would re-base every stop off a lower 11-02 fill, i.e. loosen my absolute exit levels right before AMD reports on 11-03 and ANET on 11-02/03 after the close; the current stops (NVDA ~184.5, AMD ~457, ANET ~155.5) are the pre-committed answer to a bad print and cap each earnings outcome at roughly 1-2% of NAV. The 10-year falling to a seven-week low of 4.93% is the one supportive datum for multiples and argues for patience, not churn. Not verified despite searching: the AWS growth line in Amazon's Q3 and the AMD-specific driver of its 11% drop (reported as Intel read-through and rotation); if AMD's 11-03 print shows a data-center GPU miss rather than client weakness, the stop does the work. BTC at 5% stays as the small contrarian leg at ~$77.2k.

Crypto transaction revenue fell 55% y/y, and ex-Robinhood Chain it fell 6% q/q. Net interest revenue fell 9% on lower rates and securities lending. Event contracts (+6x y/y) and options (+31%) were the only real growth lines. The stock fell about 5% after hours and is about -22% YTD; our leg is -8.46% from a pre-earnings 10-26 entry. The 'earnings-backed growth' thesis that justified the leg did not survive the print, a 12%-revenue-growth, falling-EPS broker is not a growth name, and waiting for the -18% stop would only add loss to a thesis already broken, so HOOD is exited. CRDO's fundamental story (FY2026 revenue roughly tripled, Q4 $437M, the DustPhotonics silicon-photonics acquisition) is intact, so it stays at the same 15% size and stop. positions.thesis: Credo is the cleanest earnings-backed small/mid-cap AI-connectivity name. Its active electrical cables and SerDes are being adopted across hyperscaler AI clusters, FY2026 revenue roughly tripled with a $437M Q4, and the DustPhotonics acquisition extends it into silicon photonics and optical connectivity. The stock is down about 27% over the past month on sector de-risking rather than company news, and it has held about $151 since the 10-26 entry, so I keep the same 15% at-risk size rather than adding into a tape where peer stops (ANET) are still firing. The 20% stop caps the leg's loss at about 3% of NAV, and the 50% take-profit banks a rebound toward the prior range if hyperscaler capex fears ease into December earnings.
